items.name: Leonardo da Vinci
items.blurb: Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519): Painted the Mona Lisa.
clues: He wrote his notes in mirror writing.
He drew designs for flying machines.

items.name: Michelangelo
items.blurb: Michelangelo (1475–1564): A great Italian Renaissance sculptor and painter.
clues: He designed the dome of St Peter's Basilica.
He carved the statue of David.
He painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
He was a great Italian Renaissance sculptor and painter.

items.name: Raphael
items.blurb: Raphael (1483–1520): One of the great painters of the High Renaissance.
clues: He painted The School of Athens.
He was one of the great painters of the High Renaissance.

items.name: Albrecht Dürer
items.blurb: Albrecht Dürer (1471–1528): A master of printmaking.
clues: He made a famous woodcut of a rhinoceros he never saw.
He painted a famous watercolour of a young hare.
He was a master of printmaking.

items.name: Caravaggio
items.blurb: Caravaggio (1571–1610): A rebellious Baroque painter.
clues: He killed a man and fled Rome.
He painted The Calling of Saint Matthew.
He used dramatic light and shadow.
He was a rebellious Baroque painter.

items.name: Diego Velázquez
items.blurb: Diego Velázquez (1599–1660): A great Spanish painter.
clues: He was court painter to King Philip IV.
He painted himself at work in Las Meninas.
He was a great Spanish painter.

items.name: Rembrandt
items.blurb: Rembrandt (1606–1669): A master of the Dutch Golden Age.
clues: He was a master of the Dutch Golden Age.

items.name: Johannes Vermeer
items.blurb: Johannes Vermeer (1632–1675): Painted Girl with a Pearl Earring.
clues: Only around 35 of his paintings survive.
He painted Girl with a Pearl Earring.

items.name: Francisco Goya
items.blurb: Francisco Goya (1746–1828): A Spanish court painter.
clues: He became deaf after an illness.
He painted dark pictures on the walls of his house.
He painted The Third of May 1808.
He was a Spanish court painter.

items.name: Katsushika Hokusai
items.blurb: Katsushika Hokusai (1760–1849): Made The Great Wave off Kanagawa.
clues: He used more than 30 different names.
He made a series called Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.
He was a master of woodblock prints.
He made The Great Wave off Kanagawa.

items.name: J. M. W. Turner
items.blurb: J. M. W. Turner (1775–1851): Famous for stormy seas and glowing light.
clues: He is said to have had himself tied to a ship's mast to see a storm.
He appears on the Bank of England £20 note.
He was famous for stormy seas and glowing light.

items.name: John Constable
items.blurb: John Constable (1776–1837): An English landscape painter.
clues: He painted the countryside around the River Stour.
He was an English landscape painter.

items.name: Claude Monet
items.blurb: Claude Monet (1840–1926): Painted water lilies.
clues: His painting Impression, Sunrise gave a movement its name.
He painted haystacks and cathedrals at different times of day.
He built a garden with a Japanese bridge at Giverny.

items.name: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
items.blurb: Pierre-Auguste Renoir (1841–1919): A French Impressionist.
clues: He kept painting with brushes strapped to his hands.
He painted Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette.
He painted Luncheon of the Boating Party.

img.credit: UnknownUnknown Musée d'Orsay, Dist. RMN-Grand Palais / Patrice Schmidt

items.name: Edgar Degas
items.blurb: Edgar Degas (1834–1917): Famous for paintings of ballet dancers.
clues: His eyesight failed in later life.
He made a sculpture called Little Dancer Aged Fourteen.
He is famous for paintings of ballet dancers.

items.name: Paul Cézanne
items.blurb: Paul Cézanne (1839–1906): Famous for still lifes of apples.
clues: He painted Mont Sainte-Victoire many times.
He is often called the father of modern art.
He was famous for still lifes of apples.

img.credit: Unknown; Cézanne was born in 1839 and died in 1906

items.name: Paul Gauguin
items.blurb: Paul Gauguin (1848–1903): Painted bright scenes of Polynesian life.
clues: He once worked as a stockbroker.
He lived with Van Gogh in Arles for a few weeks.
He painted bright scenes of Polynesian life.

items.name: Vincent van Gogh
items.blurb: Vincent van Gogh (1853–1890): Painted The Starry Night and Sunflowers.
clues: He sold very few paintings in his lifetime.
He cut off part of his own ear.
He painted The Starry Night and Sunflowers.

items.name: Georges Seurat
items.blurb: Georges Seurat (1859–1891): Painted with tiny dots of colour.
clues: He painted A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte.
He painted with tiny dots of colour.

items.name: Gustav Klimt
items.blurb: Gustav Klimt (1862–1918): Painted The Kiss.
clues: He painted a famous portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer.

items.name: Edvard Munch
items.blurb: Edvard Munch (1863–1944): Painted The Scream.
clues: He painted Madonna and The Sick Child.
Versions of his most famous work have been stolen twice.
He made several versions of the same famous image.

items.name: Wassily Kandinsky
items.blurb: Wassily Kandinsky (1866–1944): A pioneer of abstract art.
clues: He linked colours to musical sounds.
He was a pioneer of abstract art.

items.name: Henri Matisse
items.blurb: Henri Matisse (1869–1954): Famous for bold, bright colour.
clues: In later life he made art from painted paper cut-outs.
He led the Fauves, or wild beasts.
He was famous for bold, bright colour.

items.name: Pablo Picasso
items.blurb: Pablo Picasso (1881–1973): Co-founded Cubism.
clues: His full name has more than 20 words.
He went through a Blue Period.

items.name: Edward Hopper
items.blurb: Edward Hopper (1882–1967): Painted Nighthawks.
clues: He painted people in a late-night diner.

items.name: Georgia O'Keeffe
items.blurb: Georgia O'Keeffe (1887–1986): Painted giant close-up flowers.
clues: She was married to the photographer Alfred Stieglitz.
She painted animal skulls in the desert.

items.name: Grant Wood
items.blurb: Grant Wood (1891–1942): Painted American Gothic.
clues: His most famous models were his sister and his dentist.
He painted a farmer holding a pitchfork.

items.name: René Magritte
items.blurb: René Magritte (1898–1967): A Belgian Surrealist.
clues: He painted a pipe with the words This is not a pipe.
He painted men in bowler hats.
He painted a man with an apple in front of his face.

img.credit: Unknown authorUnknown author Restored by Giovanni Cardinali

items.name: Salvador Dalí
items.blurb: Salvador Dalí (1904–1989): A famous Surrealist.
clues: He designed the Chupa Chups logo.
He had a long, upturned moustache.
He painted melting clocks in The Persistence of Memory.

items.name: Frida Kahlo
items.blurb: Frida Kahlo (1907–1954): Painted many self-portraits with flowers in her hair.
clues: She was badly injured in a bus accident as a teenager.
She married the painter Diego Rivera.
She lived in the Blue House in Mexico City.
She painted many self-portraits with flowers in her hair.

items.name: Jackson Pollock
items.blurb: Jackson Pollock (1912–1956): A leading Abstract Expressionist.
clues: He worked with his canvases laid flat on the floor.
He was a leading Abstract Expressionist.

items.name: Roy Lichtenstein
items.blurb: Roy Lichtenstein (1923–1997): An American Pop artist.
clues: He copied the dots used in cheap printing.
He made paintings that look like comic strips.
He was an American Pop artist.

items.name: Andy Warhol
items.blurb: Andy Warhol (1928–1987): Painted Campbell's soup cans.
clues: His studio was called the Factory.
He said everyone would be famous for 15 minutes.
He made colourful prints of Marilyn Monroe.

items.name: Yayoi Kusama
items.blurb: Yayoi Kusama (1929–2026): Famous for polka dots.
clues: She has lived by choice in a psychiatric hospital in Tokyo since 1977.
She makes mirror rooms that seem to go on forever.
She is famous for polka dots.
